newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields end weaker on RBNZ statement, seen lower. [CORRECTED 06:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: NZ yields end weaker on RBNZ statement, seen lower. [CORRECTED 06:25 GMT]

text.p: 0525 GMT
* NZ short end sold sharply on RB statement
* Bonds follow suit as bearish tone pervades market
* Further weakness seen next week
* Cash at 10.00 pct vs 10.00 pct at Thursday's close
* 90 day bills 9.90 pct vs 9.81 pct
* 7/98 bond yields 8.10 pct vs 8.02 pct
* 02/01 bond yields 8.35 pct vs 8.26 pct
* 11/06 bond yields 8.37 pct vs 8.32 percent
* Dec bank bill futures -27 at 90.62, Mar -18 at 91.33
New Zealand yields closed higher (Corrects from lower) across the curve on Friday after a cautious statement from the Reserve Bank caused a rash of selling, particularly of bill future contracts.

In its September Economic Projections, the central bank forecast underlying inflation to peak at 2.7 percent in the September 1996 quarter before falling to 2.1 percent in the March 1997 year and 0.8 percent in 1998.

"It was reasonably bearish," a bill trader said of the forecasts. "Most people seemed to have priced in a reasonably positive statement and for further-out underlying inflation to be a fair bit lower, but it didn't come to that."
December futures were hit particularly hard, ending 27 points weaker at 90.62. The 90-day bank bill yield rose about nine points to 9.90 percent.
The market had been anticipating an easing in monetary conditions by early next year, but the Reserve Bank said it saw no scope for an easing before late in 1997.
"An easing is off the agenda until conclusive evidence is at hand that inflation will in fact fall away sharply next year and beyond," the bank said.
While economists said they expected a market-driven easing as early as late this year in spite of the bank's comments, dealers said the short-term outlook was for further weakness.
"I think from here we'll probably see some more selling," a dealer said.
Weakness in the short end flowed through to the rest of the curve, with bond yields spiking between five and nine basis points.

"The bond market is weaker right across the yield curve after the Reserve Bank forecasts," a bond dealer said. "Bank bills were led weaker by bank bill futures selling, which has spilled out right across the yield curve."
He said closing sentiment looked a little bearish. "I wouldn't be surprised to see further weakness," he said.
-- Matthew Brockett (64 4) 473-3736
